Hi Alice — great meeting today, thanks for the time. 

Quick recap + proposed next steps from our call: 

1) Goals we agreed on
- Use tool/function calling for structured enrichment (payments lookup, balance fetch) and orchestration (open ticket, trigger workflow).
- Prefer server-side tool execution (for credentialed calls) with the model returning structured tool arguments.

2) Integration scope for MVP
- SDK setup (Node + Python): quickstart + sample tool definitions
- Auth: OAuth2 for FinApps systems + signed service-to-service tokens for Redwood private connectors
- Routing: latency-first for interactive UI (US region) but fallback to cheaper model variants for background jobs
- Embeddings/rerankers: semantic retrieval for knowledge ops; rerank candidates post-embedding match for business rules
- Error handling: explicit tool_error schema + retries for idempotent calls; circuit-breaker for downstream latency spikes

3) Next steps (action owners & timeline)

Subject: Technical follow-up: tool definitions, parallel tools, error handling patterns

Hi Alice — looping in a few detailed patterns we discussed. Below are pragmatic, implementation-focused recommendations you can use during your spike.

1) Tool definitions (example contract) - Define tools as typed function specs; model returns JSON that matches the tool schema. Example (pseudo):
{
  "tool": "get_account_balance",
  "args": {"account_id": "string", "as_of": "ISO8601"}
}

Key points:
- Keep arg schemas explicit and small to reduce hallucinations.
- Prefer enums for action types when possible.

2) Tool choice & orchestration - Single responsibility: each tool does one backend action (e.g., fetch_balance, create_ticket, enrich_customer).
- Controller layer (server) receives model output, validates against tool schema, then executes.
- For orchestrations that require multiple tools, use an ordered plan: model returns sequence of tool calls with context.

3) Parallel tools pattern
- Use when independent data can be fetched concurrently (e.g., balances + open_tickets + recent_transactions).
- Implement as fan-out on the server: validate all tool args then execute in parallel with bounded concurrency.
- Collate results and send a short summary back to the model for final aggregation or for direct UI rendering.

4) Structured output & rerankers
- Prefer model-suggested candidates + deterministic reranker on server to enforce business rules.
- Example flow: embedding search -> top-N candidates -> reranker scoring (business_score + relevance_score) -> return top-K to UI.

5) Error handling
- Tool-level errors: return a typed error object to the controller (error_code, message, retryable).
- Retry policy: retry only for idempotent ops (GET, safe POST) with exponential backoff, max 3 attempts.
- Fallbacks: on persistent failure, model should be informed with a tool_error object so it can suggest alternatives or user-facing messaging.
- Circuit-breaker: open when downstream error rate > threshold for X seconds, route requests to degraded mode (cached responses or alternate model).

6) Auth & security notes
- Keep credential exchange server-side; never embed long-lived secrets in model prompts.
- Signed assertions (JWTs) for short-lived service tokens when the model suggests a service action.

Attachments: attached a short architecture excerpt (integration-patterns.pdf) and SDK snippets in redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip.

If you can share sandbox endpoints and a sample account_id, I’ll put together a spike PR with concrete code for Node + Python.

Thanks,
